pr_body:
This is a proposed fix for #511 & #510.

Runtime code generation is loaded in the GrainFactory and kept current as new assemblies are loaded. `IGrainMethodInvoker` implementations are also loaded in `GrainTypeManager` upon initialization.

Roslyn is used for generating `GrainReference`s and `IGrainMethodInvoker`s and not for generating `GrainReference` serializers, `Cast` methods, or `CreateObjectRefernce`/`DeleteObjectReference` methods . Instead, Expression Trees are used in those cases. In the case of `GrainReference` casters, they of course rely on having a generated `GrainReference` with the correct marker attribute.

Marker attributes (`MethodInvokerAttribute` and `GrainReferenceAttribute`) have been changed to include a `GrainType` parameter which takes the (possibly generic) type of the grain which they relate to.

This is implemented as an optional plugin for Orleans. If `OrleansCodeGenerator.dll` is present at runtime, it will be loaded and used. If it is not present, the existing mechanism of compile-time code generation will have to suffice instead.

I have not created a NuGet package, so if this is the approach we are going to take, that will need to be done before the PR is ready to merge.

All criticism is welcome :)

We may need to add an attribute to allow to explicitly exclude certain types from codegen. Investigating test failures, I found that we have several test grain interfaces defined with intentional violations of the rules (properties, methods returning types other than Task, etc.). Codegen doesn't run against them today because these interface are not in the test grain interfaces assembly. But now test silo blows up because the run time codegen fails, legitimately, to generate code artefacts for them on startup. If we could mark these interfaces with an "ignore" attribute for codegen, that would solve the problem.

I'll try to exclude these test interface for now to see what else breaks.
I submitted https://github.com/dotnet/orleans/pull/640 with tests that were blowing up with this PR.
Here's how to repro the issue. With https://github.com/dotnet/orleans/pull/640 merged, add a test as follows to TesterInternal.

``` csharp
[TestMethod, TestCategory("BVT"), TestCategory("Functional"), TestCategory("Codegen")]
public void CodegenAgainstTestAssembly()
{
        var asm = Assembly.GetExecutingAssembly();
        GrainMethodInvokerGenerator.GenerateAndLoadForAssembly(asm);
}
```

The behavior in my test runs appears non-deterministic, with `GenerateAndLoadForAssembly()` being called or not against the test assembly. It is interesting why. But the above test forces it explicitly.
The good news is that with the offending grain interfaces removed, I got only one failure out of 458 tests, and it looks unrelated. I'll play more with it, will try disabling compile time codegen, check logs, etc. Looks good so far.

In the latest push, I have implemented a generated assembly cache to speed up test runs which use an `AppDomain` per test.
Basically it works by copying the generated assemblies out of a silo's `AppDomain` after is has initially loaded & on shutdown into the test runner's `AppDomain`.
When a silo is being loaded in a new `AppDomain`, we prime the `CodeGenerator` with the cached assemblies so that when they are demanded, they can be loaded without performing expensive type analysis and compilation.

There is a `SkipCodeGeneration` attribute which consumers can use to opt-out of runtime code generation.

EDIT: Median test time is ~2 seconds.
